content.text: {"prompt": "A square abstract expressionist painting that fills the entire canvas edge to edge, with no frame, border, wall, room, or gallery setting. It is purely nonrepresentational, with no recognizable objects, figures, faces, bodies, scenes, landscapes, horizons, machines, diagrams, symbols, icons, letters, numbers, or text. The left half is dense, turbulent, and layered: heavy impasto strokes of burnt orange, hot vermilion, and bruised magenta, scraped and dragged in fast diagonal gestures that crowd and press against each other. Beneath them, thin scumbled glazes of ultramarine and ink-black show through in torn patches. This pressure builds toward the center. There it meets a long, steady, vertical-leaning sweep of cool pale celadon and chalky off-white, laid down in a single deliberate pull of a wide palette knife. The sweep holds its line against the surrounding heat without being overwhelmed. To the right the painting opens into slow, quiet fields of translucent grey-green and soft blue, thinly washed with visible canvas weave and faint drips, with generous empty space that lets the eye rest. Scattered through that calm are a few small, stubborn, unresolved clusters of dense saturated crimson, rough and thick, which refuse to blend into the cool surround and stay sharply present. The rhythm moves from frantic and staccato on the left to measured and exhaling on the right. Spatial tension comes from the collision of warm and cool and from the contrast of thick, scraped texture with thin, luminous transparency. Visible bristle marks, palette-knife ridges, dry-brush skips, and layered overpainting give an honest, tactile, handmade surface. The mood is strained but steady, with clarity, restraint, and a quiet insistence on what remains unfinished. Rich oil-paint texture, natural soft light, high detail, no vignette."}
